item.title: Rice prices surge despite record government stocks as southern varieties nearly double
item.description: Prices for rice in southern India have nearly doubled, driven by a decrease in overall production and increased demand. The worst monsoon rainfall in over a decade has negatively impacted yields of premium non-basmati varieties. Government rice stocks remain at a record high, but do not match regional consumer preferences. Suggested government interventions aim to increase domestic availability and control unsustainable price increases.

item.title: Govt projects Kharif foodgrain production at 167.14 mln tonnes despite El Nino; 2025-26 crop output a record
item.description: Kharif foodgrain production for the 2026-27 crop year is projected at 167.14 million tonnes amid weather challenges. Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced these estimates despite El Nino and a delayed monsoon. In the previous crop year, foodgrain production reached a record high of 378.54 million tonnes. Additionally, pulses and oilseeds are being prioritized due to India's reliance on imports.

item.title: India’s foodgrain production rises to record 378.54 MT in 2025-26
item.description: According to the final crop estimates for 2025-26, rice production increased by 4.97 million tonnes to a record 155.15 million tonnes, compared with 150.18 million tonnes in 2024-25.

item.title: India's sugar production to fall 5.4% to 265 lakh tonnes in 2026-27: ISMA
item.description: Sugarcane acreage during the current season is estimated at 55.53 lakh hectares, down 3.2% from 57.35 lakh hectares in 2025-26.

item.title: Maharashtra Cabinet approves free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh farmers, Rs 5,548 crore for Narmada-Tapi project
item.description: The Maharashtra Cabinet on Wednesday approved free foodgrains for 42.30 lakh farmers, ₹5,548 crore for the Narmada-Tapi Valley Diversion Project and a draft bill to regulate private aided schools, among 14 decisions taken at the meeting.
